applies_why: The rule governs whether a single verse that states no link can ground a STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED verdict, and the judge text grounds an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on a single verse's grammar.
quote: the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.
room: Whether a verse whose wording 'admits both readings' counts as stating a link or its contrary, or whether the judge's citation of the defender's and challenger's multi-verse answers makes the verdict rest on the chain rather than on the single verse; I weighed the first reading as decisive because the stated ground is the single verse's grammar.
why: The judge's only stated ground for UNDERDETERMINED is the grammar of one verse, Matthew 1:16, which by its own description admits two readings and so states neither a link nor its contrary, which the rule forbids as a ground.
